# XDR404: contract event topics or data trusted by position or kind without a shape or emitter check

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | XDR4xx: assumptions about the ledger's form, ranges and outcomes |
| How to fix | check len(topics) and each value's Type (or use Get<Arm>() and its ok) before reading it, or first compare the event's ContractId with the contract whose event shape you rely on |
| Default severity | error (`severity: {XDR404: …}` changes it) |
| Default rule set | yes |
| Guide | [Contract events](../../guide/indexer-hardening.mdx#fields-events) |
| Self-audit checklist item | HC-306 |
| Demonstrating corpus entry | `cap-0046/event-topic-count-extremes` (registered in [corpus/plan.json](../../corpus/plan.json)) |
| Fixtures | [lint/testdata/xdr4xx/xdr404](../testdata/xdr4xx/xdr404) |

## What it reports

A contract event's topics or data read by position or kind with no shape check and no check of the emitting
contract:

- `topics[k]` with a constant `k`, with no enclosing or earlier check that mentions `len(topics)` (directly, or
  through a variable set under such a check);
- `v.Must<Arm>()` on a topic, the data or a value read from them, with no check of `v.Type` or `v.Get<Arm>()`.

Event values are the `Topics` and `Data` fields of `xdr.ContractEventV0` and what is read from them, and
parameters named `topics` or `data` of type `xdr.ScVal`, `[]xdr.ScVal` or `xdr.ScVec`. A dominating comparison of
the event's `ContractId` with something other than `nil` fixes the shape to that contract's and silences the
report.

## Why it matters

Any contract can emit any number of topics of any type. A reader that indexes `topics[2]` or calls `MustSym()`
panics on the first event that does not have the shape it expected; a reader that stops on a panic halts the
whole pipeline on an event anyone can emit.

## Example

Reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr4xx/xdr404/bad.go
// (a) A fixed position read with no length check: a contract that emits one
// topic panics the reader.
func eventName(ev xdr.ContractEvent) string {
	topics := ev.Body.V0.Topics
	sym, ok := topics[1].GetSym()
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	return string(sym)
}
```

Not reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr4xx/xdr404/good.go
// Length and type checked.
func eventNameChecked(ev xdr.ContractEvent) string {
	topics := ev.Body.V0.Topics
	if len(topics) < 2 {
		return ""
	}
	sym, ok := topics[1].GetSym()
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	return string(sym)
}
```

## Limits

The length check is matched by how the slice is written; a check made by the caller is not seen. Transaction-level
events (which only the host emits) are treated like contract events.

## Configure and suppress

Turn the rule off by leaving XDR404 out of `rules` in `.xdrlint.yml` or a profile. To accept one report, put `//xdrlint:ignore XDR404 <reason>` on the reported line or on the enclosing function's doc comment (under golangci-lint, `//nolint:xdrlint // <reason>`), or add an entry to an external suppression file for code you cannot edit. A suppression needs a reason, and one that suppresses nothing is itself reported (XDR000). See [Configuring and suppressing](README.md#linter-suppressions).
